title: The map on dual-number tangent vectors induced by a morphism is linear
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $x\in X$ and $y=f(x)$, such that the induced map of residue fields $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism; identify $\kappa(y)$ with $\kappa=\kappa(x)$ through it, and accordingly the dual numbers $\kappa(y)[\epsilon]$ with $\kappa[\epsilon]$ [def-sc-dual-numbers]. Let $T_X$ and $T_Y$ be the $\kappa$-vector spaces of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]\to X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at $x$, resp. $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]\to Y$ at $y$, given by [lem-sc-tangent-space-vector-space]. Then for every $\theta\in T_X$ the composite $f\circ\theta$ lies in $T_Y$, and $\theta\mapsto f\circ\theta$ is a $\kappa$-linear map $T_X\to T_Y$.

source.place: Tag 0B2F, varieties-lemma-map-tangent-spaces (the natural linear map df), with S = Spec k

proof.text: Write $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ and $j_y:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$ for the canonical point morphisms. The residue-field naturality statement [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], applied to $f$ at $x$, says $f\circ j_x=j_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x))$. Under the assumed identification of these fields the right side is $j_y$. If $c:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon]$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\epsilon\mapsto0$ (as in [lem-sc-tangent-space-vector-space]) and $\theta\circ c=j_x$, associativity gives $(f\circ\theta)\circ c=j_y$. Thus composition with $f$ maps $T_X$ into $T_Y$.

source.place: Tag 0B2F, lemma-map-tangent-spaces (proof omitted); base-point verification using Schemes Tag 01J5

proof.text: For $\lambda\in\kappa$ and $\theta\in T_X$, scalar multiplication is precomposition with $\operatorname{Spec}(m_\lambda)$, where $m_\lambda(\epsilon)=\lambda\epsilon$ [lem-sc-tangent-space-vector-space]. Hence $f\circ(\lambda\theta)=f\circ\theta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(m_\lambda)=\lambda(f\circ\theta)$, using the same residue-field identification for $T_Y$. This includes $\lambda=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B2B, lemma-tangent-space, scalar multiplication; Tag 0B2F, lemma-map-tangent-spaces

proof.text: For $\theta_1,\theta_2\in T_X$, let $\Theta$ be the unique map from $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]$ whose restrictions along $j_i$ are $\theta_i$, as supplied by the pushout statement [lem-sc-tangent-space-vector-space]. The restrictions of $f\circ\Theta$ along the same $j_i$ are $f\circ\theta_i$; uniqueness in that statement therefore identifies it with the map used to form $(f\circ\theta_1)+(f\circ\theta_2)$ in $T_Y$. Precomposing both with $s$ gives $f\circ(\theta_1+\theta_2)=(f\circ\theta_1)+(f\circ\theta_2)$. Together with step 2 and step 1, composition with $f$ is a $\kappa$-linear map.

lean.statement: theorem exists_tangentMap_linear (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (x : X) (he : Function.Bijective (f.residueFieldMap x).hom) : let KX := X.residueField x let KY := Y.residueField (f x) let DX := Spec (.of (DualNumber KX)) let DY := Spec (.of (DualNumber KY)) let cX : Spec KX ⟶ DX := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom KX KX KX).toRingHom) let cY : Spec KY ⟶ DY := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom KY KY KY).toRingHom) let qX : DX ⟶ Spec KX := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.inlHom KX KX)) let qY : DY ⟶ Spec KY := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TrivSqZeroExt.inlHom KY KY)) let bX := X.fromSpecResidueField x let bY := Y.fromSpecResidueField (f x) let TX := {θ : DX ⟶ X // cX ≫ θ = bX ∧ θ ≫ pX = qX ≫ bX ≫ pX} let TY := {θ : DY ⟶ Y // cY ≫ θ = bY ∧ θ ≫ pY = qY ≫ bY ≫ pY} let hX := (exists_tangentVectors_vectorSpace k X pX x).2.2.2 let hY := (exists_tangentVectors_vectorSpace k Y pY (f x)).2.2.2 letI : AddCommGroup TX := Classical.choose hX letI : AddCommGroup TY := Classical.choose hY letI : Module KX TX := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec hX) letI : Module KY TY := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec hY) let e : KY ≃+* KX := RingEquiv.ofBijective (f.residueFieldMap x).hom he letI : Module KX TY := Module.compHom TY e.symm.toRingHom let d : DY ⟶ DX := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (DualNumber.mapRingHom e.symm.toRingHom)) ∃ L : TX →ₗ[KX] TY, ∀ θ : TX, (L θ).val = d ≫ θ.val ≫ f
